selection_definition: First three exercise details in actual document order, cross-checked against current Source91 inventory ordinals.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 10.B1 — Medium: Reserve space for a noisier sensor
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current paragraph has the right numerical answer but jumps from sensor subtraction to the command bound. Explain the disturbance integral, why the affine lower bound controls the entire hold, actuator intersection, nearest-point selection, correction and explicit terminal arithmetic.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 10.B2 — Hard: A safe set can demand an unavailable actuator
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The feasibility answer and missing-control-direction conclusion are correct, but a beginning student needs the actual interval intersection, inequality rearrangement, equality endpoint and a trajectory showing why any positive hold fails at zero clearance. Separate temporary help from faster sampling at positive clearance from the impossibility of indefinite robustness.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 10.B3 — Hard: Add the age of a measurement to its error budget
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The numerical values 0.14, -0.32 and -0.09 are right but the answer omits the triangle inequality connecting an old reading to the present state, the held-input derivation and actuator projection. Spell out these steps and keep the caveat about the past speed bound.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise P1.B1 — Medium: The upper boundary needs its own filter
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer starts from the actual 9.8-litre measurement and derives the compatible-state interval, adds both disturbance endpoints and solves both safety inequalities. It explicitly intersects the resulting interval with actuator limits, explains why the closest action is the upper feasible endpoint, computes the 0.8 correction and evaluates the two attained next-volume extremes. The upper-boundary trap and modeled scope are made explicit.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise P1.B2 — Hard: A larger inflow can destroy recursive feasibility
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The larger-disturbance solution derives 1.3 combined uncertainty and both next-volume endpoints, rearranges their inequalities, substitutes the valid x=0,y=-0.1 boundary measurement and exhibits the empty actuator intersection. It then checks the actual true-boundary obstruction u≥1.2 separately, so a student can distinguish conservative interval failure from genuine lack of robust control and understand why improved sensing does not restore recursive feasibility.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise P1.B3 — Hard: Write the quantifiers in the right order
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer defines the entire reachable measurement interval Y and compatible-state set X(y), writes all quantifiers with u(y) chosen before x,w, and explains each information dependency. It verifies nonempty safety/actuator intersection for every y using endpoint bounds and width, justifies repeating the implication, and proves that a single constant input fails by incompatible lower- and upper-boundary requirements. Every quantifier and feedback distinction requested is worked through.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 8.B1 — Medium: Reprice a tighter operating budget
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer states the discounted linear reward/cost model, subtracts and divides the new budget inequality to p≤1/4, uses positive reward slope to select the endpoint, and substitutes both resulting returns. It parameterizes the value for every interior budget and derives the same multiplier both by its derivative and by the zero Lagrangian slope. Its positive one-step cost example correctly distinguishes an expected discounted allowance from zero pathwise violations.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 8.B2 — Hard: Change the discount without changing the meaning by accident
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The discount calculation explicitly changes the geometric weighting from 10 to 20, derives both affine totals, solves the new feasible mixture and substitutes the 50-point reward. It evaluates the reused 4/9 mixture to cost 2 and explains the equivalent per-step allowance (1−γ)d, including the budget 2 needed to preserve the old operational interpretation. This covers the requested mixture, reuse failure and modeling reason with intermediate algebra rather than only final values.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 8.B3 — Hard: A monitoring variable is part of the decision
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The rescaled-budget answer establishes the admissibility inequality before testing 0.5 and 0.6, computes z 3 with a common denominator and division by 9/10, and independently checks all original-time costs plus γ³z 3=0.015. It also computes the inadmissible spend 1.066 and distinguishes deterministic realized-cost bookkeeping from uncertain pathwise obligations. The state variable, time scale and every requested calculation are explicit.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 6.B1 — Medium: Choose the monitoring period
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer recomputes both weighted-distance terms with units, identifies localization and motion reserves, writes and solves the certificate inequality by subtracting 0.27 and dividing by positive 0.8, then evaluates the requested 0.2-second proposal. It interprets the interval as observation plus computation/switching, includes the remaining 0.0025-second timing budget, and distinguishes nonnegative recovery at equality from strict clearance.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 6.B2 — Hard: Use a library of recovery regions
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: Every requested state/backup pair has its own coordinate differences, velocity weighting, summed distance, reserve and comparison. The successful second backup gives an explicit 0.05-metre recovery margin; the faster state is checked against both backup centers and remains uncertified. The closing explanation correctly uses the union of separately witnessed certificates and does not infer interpolation or safety from position alone.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 6.P1 — Easy: Safety is the minimum along a trajectory
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current solution lists four margins but omits the absolute-value substitutions. The first easy problem should show each evaluation, distinguish the finite sampled minimum from the all-time requirement and evaluate the supplied intermediate violation explicitly.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 1.B1 — Medium: Budget a fleet demonstration
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The solution defines all twenty failure events and the fleet complement, writes each union-bound inequality, converts the 0.95 success target to 0.05 total failure, solves 20δ≤0.05 and checks the resulting 0.0025 allocation. It then derives the independent-complement product, evaluates 0.9975^20 and distinguishes a lower bound from equality and from a shared-error dependent model. Every requested allocation, independence case and interpretation is present.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 1.B2 — Hard: A rare spike changes the chosen specification
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The solution works all three specifications separately: expands the mean arithmetic, identifies precisely the 109-degree overheating atom, fills the worst 5% with 2% hot plus 3% ordinary mass, and calculates the 79-degree tail average. It also derives and minimizes the piecewise CVaR variational objective on all ν regions, treats the discrete atom correctly, and explains why the mean accepts while both risk constraints reject. No derivation or requested comparison is compressed into an unexplained result.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 1.P1 — Easy: Read a safe set
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The existing answer is mathematically correct, but the opening exercise can show the algebra leading to the interval and the actual squaring/subtraction at each tested state. Expand those intermediate evaluations, then explain the induction obligation and explicit safe-to-unsafe counterexample.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 13.B1 — Medium: Check whether the target response is expressible
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer rewrites the physical target in normalized coordinates using both scale factors, derives its coefficient-gradient norm with intermediate squares, and constructs an actual short increment in the maximizing direction inside the open region. The ratio proves a necessary 0.400005 gain, rather than merely citing a gradient or optimization failure, and the interpretation clearly locates the incompatible specification.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 13.B2 — Hard: Reserve gain for approximate orthogonality
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The six-stage answer defines the implementation error, uses orthogonality and the triangle inequality to obtain each 1.002 norm, multiplies all stage/activation/readout gains, and solves the external scale bound with signed/nonnegative cases. It tests the original physical sensor-error budget again and distinguishes an exact spectral-error assumption from entrywise or approximate claims, so the requested sufficient scale has a complete derivation.

exercise_assessments.label: Easy 1 — Normalize with the correct side of an estimate
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current three-step answer states that the exact spectral norm is 3 but does not show how the diagonal matrix produces it or why scalar division scales that norm. Add the maximum-gain derivation, both explicit normalized matrices and the Frobenius calculation, preserving the distinction between a lower estimate and certified upper denominator.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 12.B1 — Medium: Return to physical sensor errors
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer propagates both hardware scales with units and exact corner radius, applies the squared-SDP-to-Lipschitz conversion and physical output factor, and correctly identifies 0.065320 as a failed sufficient bound rather than an actual violation. It then enumerates regional gradients, derives the box/ℓ1 bound, handles segments crossing activation boundaries and supplies an attaining perturbation, so the non-strict 0.06 allowance and the optional stricter SDP-only calibration are fully distinguished.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 12.B2 — Hard: Audit an attractive coupled multiplier
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The multiplier test independently proves PSD by T=aaᵀ, evaluates both actual ReLU vectors, forms every increment and remainder, multiplies T by that remainder and gets the explicit−2 violation. It explains why PSD does not justify a bilinear activation QC, why a feasible LMI cannot repair a false prerequisite, and why diagonal nonnegative incremental multipliers differ from nonincremental repeated-nonlinearity statements. This addresses the requested numerical test and certificate consequence step by step.

exercise_assessments.label: Easy 1 — A radius in two norms
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The original radius formulas are right but introduce the crucial √2 logit-gap bound without derivation, and skip the three-coordinate norm comparison. Show the coefficient vector and Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, the positive-margin rearrangement, the squared-norm bound, and both strict boundary cases.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 11.B1 — Medium: Diagnose a larger learned-controller error
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current paragraph states radius 0.18, nominal 0.82 and physical 0.59 without deriving the changed error recurrence or explaining tube versus physical-state invariance. Show controller substitution, the disturbance/approximation triangle bound, the deviation equation, the radius inequality and the nominal containment calculation.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 11.B2 — Hard: Design to an accuracy requirement
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The original answer substitutes the requested radius but omits the full recurrence and why selecting the largest radius allowance produces the maximal uniform error budget. Show the inequality rearrangement, feasible nonnegative error range, nominal tightening, and explain the pointwise quantifier that mean squared error lacks.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 11.B3 — Hard: A rare approximation error defeats an average-error argument
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The correct original values are listed in one paragraph. Expand the uniform-density interval probability, the mixture/integral for squared error, taking its square root only afterward, the attained maximum, and the independent-test complement/product. Keep the important distinction between failing this uniform-approximation specification and proving a closed-loop safety violation.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 14.B1 — Medium: Carry a bounded sensor bias through feedback
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current expanded answer has the correct four results, but the ultimate bound skips the first recurrence substitutions and finite geometric-sum denominator, and checks the actuator only after declaring invariance. Derive the bias disturbance decomposition, verify actuator applicability on the same region, prove the induction, then unroll the inequality and translate its limit into temperature units.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 14.B2 — Hard: A stable delayed loop can leave the temperature box
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The delayed-state answer derives the augmented matrix determinant and discriminant, gives both complex roots and their squared magnitude, and states the linear discrete-time stability implication. It separately evaluates an explicitly allowed independently initialized memory pair, checks its 0.6 successor and 0.75-kilowatt initial actuator command, and respects the question’s no-prehistory qualifier. Thus convergence is not confused with square containment and each requested calculation is visible.

exercise_assessments.label: Easy 1 — Find the equilibrium before shifting
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current result is right but compresses controller substitution, equilibrium rearrangement and cancellation into short assertions. Show the full affine closed loop, solve and verify both equilibrium coordinates, expand the shifted dynamics, and test the unshifted origin directly.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 9.B1 — Medium: Explain the metric before computing a step
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer explicitly fixes g,H,δ and the cost residual, then computes both Euclidean lengths, both weighted quadratic trust costs with the 1/2 factor, both reward dot products and both cost residuals. It checks inside/boundary distinctions and explains why equal ordinary distance does not equal trust cost or local feasibility; true-controller safety remains a separate statement.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 9.B2 — Hard: Check the price of an active constraint
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The KKT answer uses the required maximization sign, computes Hs and b, solves λ from the second coordinate and ν from the first, and proves positivity. Both complementary-slackness residuals are evaluated explicitly, with primal and dual feasibility checked. The two prices are tied to their exact local right-hand-side resources and the answer explicitly excludes nonlinear remainder, estimated gradients and physical-safety claims.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 9.B3 — Hard: Build a less coarse sufficient constraint
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer names U and its upper-bound hypothesis before substituting either point. It derives the original norm 7/25 and residual 7/125, computes the conservative norm 1/4 and−3/20 residual, distinguishes failure to certify from actual violation, and revisits both conclusions under the requested equality hypothesis. Every test, sign and interpretation follows from the displayed inequality.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 5.B1 — Medium: Certify the gain the actuator might implement
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The correct command interval is stated compactly. Explain why interval containment reduces to the two endpoint inequalities, rearrange each, test the actual allowed 1.6 realization and distinguish being outside a certified union from proved physical unsafety. Show the inclusive/strict-headroom boundary conventions.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 5.B2 — Hard: Replace deterministic noise by a finite-run event
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The existing solution correctly handles conditional adaptive noise and the union bound, but compresses the logarithm/reversal/square-root steps into a verbal instruction and gives the final cone radius directly. Show the tower expectation, union-bound budget, every algebraic transformation to E and the observation-based radius, retaining finite-horizon conditional assumptions and the independent safe seed.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 5.P1 — Easy: Build one LoSBO safety cone
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The opening easy answer gives the right interval but omits the chain from noisy observation to Lipschitz transfer and the domain intersection, and evaluates 0.65 without its 0.25 distance. Display the lower bound and inequality rearrangement, both distances and endpoints, and clarify that a below-threshold lower certificate is not an actual unsafe value.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 4.B1 — Medium: Keep heat and vibration constraints separate
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current answer has the right radii but jumps directly to transferred margins and calls a negative lower bound a failed proposal without distinguishing uncertified from actually unsafe. Derive the Lipschitz lower-bound transfer, apply each physical unit separately, solve both radius inequalities and inspect the intersection and equality.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 4.B2 — Hard: Account for imperfect gain realization
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The existing paragraph gives d≤0.26 and the failed 0.28 example, but a beginning reader benefits from explicit implemented-gain notation, triangle inequality, both uncertainty-robust conditions and comparison with the positive nominal margin. Preserve the distinction between a negative certificate lower bound and an actual violation.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 4.P1 — Easy: True safety and a noisy measurement
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer computes the actual noisy observation 0.1−0.2=−0.1, separately compares the given true value against the safety threshold, and provides a positive-observation counterexample with f=−0.1 and noise 0.2. It names the missing lower-bound/noise-confidence evidence and correctly requires that evidence before execution. This small first exercise already shows both sign cases and why observing a value differs from certifying the underlying query.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 3.B1 — Medium: Repeat a measurement before heating
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The repeated-location calculation explicitly defines the all-ones vector, its dimension, K=4·11ᵀ and λ=1. It verifies the eigen-direction solve with 1ᵀ1=3 and 13·1, justifies uniqueness by positive definiteness, performs both posterior solves and every 24/13 and 4/13 substitution, takes the square root with units, and checks the 59.955554-degree conditional upper temperature. It distinguishes latent uncertainty, independent repeats and the separate original dataset, so the supplied confidence event is not silently proved.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 3.B2 — Hard: A calibration discrepancy survives the posterior
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current paragraph states the final upper envelope and nominal threshold without showing why a bounded discrepancy is added with its worst sign. Write the two separate bounds, their sum, the failed old inequality and rearrangement for the largest replacement; preserve the confidence-event and systematic-discrepancy limitations.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 3.P1 — Easy: A two-point kernel matrix
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The present answer identifies both eigenvalues and the correct evaluations/norm, but skips the matrix-vector products and the reproducing inner-product connection to cᵀKc. Show the two independent eigenvectors, the signed kernel evaluations, Kc and the final dot product, then explain why coefficient length is different.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 2.B1 — Medium: Certify a rectangular startup specification
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The solution squares and sums both startup-coordinate bounds, shows the 0.98 maximum and disk containment, derives coordinate magnitude from the Euclidean norm, identifies the symmetric A eigenvalues and contraction q, and propagates the worst radius. It also computes sharper row-wise 0.49/0.56 bounds and translates them to the stated temperature units while explaining the locally valid-model induction. These are actual intermediate steps for all requested bounds.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 2.B2 — Hard: Replace convergence by a disturbance tube
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The disturbance answer derives the norm recurrence by two explicit inequalities, maximizes it on a radius-R disk, rearranges and rationalizes R*=0.05/(1−q), and retains the operating-box restriction R≤1. It tests the unit disk, unrolls the recurrence and finite geometric sum, gives the ultimate rather than finite-entry conclusion, and constructs a nonzero equilibrium along the q eigenvector that both disproves universal convergence and proves smaller disks fail. No missing requested case remains.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 2.P1 — Easy: KKT with one active constraint
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The original answer picks the nearest feasible point and verifies KKT, but does not solve the complementary-slackness alternatives. Show all four conditions, rule out an inactive bound by its infeasible stationary point, solve the active branch for λ, and give an elementary global/unique-optimum check alongside curvature.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 15.B1 — Medium: Reverify after the input envelope changes
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The answer determines the first unit stays active, identifies the only remaining breakpoint, simplifies both affine branches, evaluates their endpoint ranges and names the attained global extrema. It applies the exact 0.3 maximum to 59.7 and explicitly treats equality, zero margin, the changed negative minimum and the excluded residual. The claimed deterministic range is justified by exhaustive branches rather than sampled endpoints.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 15.B2 — Hard: Calibrate a whole ten-step forecast
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The solution explains the integer-ceiling condition, rearranges the 0.99(n+1) requirement to n≥99, and checks the boundary order statistic. It defines calibration objects as whole trajectories and connects the max-score event to all ten residual bounds, then adds both neural and residual allowances to 59.35 and states the 0.03 margin. It correctly limits coverage to a marginal exchangeability guarantee and contrasts it with the 0.90 pointwise union bound.

exercise_assessments.label: Easy 1 — Turn a label claim into a scalar specification
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The correct current answer compresses the logit subtraction and monotonicity into p=1−3x, and gives logits(1,2) without their forward substitutions. Expand the scalar violation construction, endpoint/worst-case calculation, tie threshold and actual counterexample; keep the distinction between a positive sound upper bound and proof of failure.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 7.B1 — Medium: A looser temperature cap may not help
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The relaxed-cap answer defines K0, follows the synchronous pruning rule to remove 62 in the first round and 60 in the second, and explains why 60 initially survived. It verifies at least one surviving action for every remaining state and the fixed point K3=K2, establishing maximal continued feasibility rather than just a safe subset. The unchanged interlock and the practical difference between delaying failure and sustaining operation are explicit.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 7.B2 — Hard: Recompute the penalty after changing the horizon preference
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The current answer derives the penalty threshold correctly but asserts that the alternative cooling detour at 56 is worse without comparing its discounted rewards, and compresses the threshold fraction rearrangement. Add the actual same-state three-step route comparison, safe Bellman values, complete unsafe return, inequality algebra and equality/24 checks so the optimal-action conclusion follows step by step.

exercise_assessments.label: Exercise 7.P1 — Easy: Safe now, but doomed next
exercise_assessments.thoroughness_rationale: The correct verbal classification can be made more traceable at this first easy exercise by showing the initial nonfailure set, its one-round pruning and fixed point, then testing both actions at A against the resulting kernel and the two-step failure of go.

assessment_criteria: Actual method and why it answers the question
Explicit symbols, assumptions and physical/statistical units
Intermediate calculations, substitutions or logical implications
Reasons for substantive steps and requested boundary/case treatment
Result interpretation and limits of the certificate

actual_candidate_browser_QA.visual_scope: One full-page landscape screenshot was inspected to confirm explorer/layout rendering. The very long whole-page image does not provide a readable visual inspection of every replacement. Automated KaTeX/expanded-overflow checks cover all changed pages; independent readable-view review remains with integration.

scope: Read-only/candidate authoring for48 non-primer DOM openings, using exact current Source91 questions/hints/bodies and authored mirrors. All23 replacements are substantive exercise-specific reasoning;25 retains are individually justified. Integration and independent review happen separately after the frozen formal work.
